chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) ruled: 'There is no guarantee (for the buyer) in the manumission of a slave, unless the buyer stipulates it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on guaranteeing a slave's value if they are manumitted after sale?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the default position in commercial transactions, establishing that the guarantee of value (uhdah) for a manumitted slave is not automatic but contingent upon explicit stipulation by the buyer. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'al-asl al-bar'ah' (presumption of innocence/exemption from liability) in sales, where obligations are not assumed unless specified. It highlights the precision of early Imamic legal reasoning in distinguishing between inherent defects and contractual conditions.
